# Question

Which survey responses distinguish reported Trump voters from other presidential
voters among Latinos in the 2020 CMPS? Three nested models describe the full
predictive structure, then the structure remaining after withholding information
close to the electoral choice and direct partisan attachment. This post-election
analysis describes predictive associations, not causes of vote choice.

```{r}
#| label: source-sample-policy
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(ranger);library(treeshap)})
stopifnot(requireNamespace("digest",quietly=TRUE))
source_root<-Sys.getenv("CMPS2020_SOURCE","/Users/jessala/Desktop/Active/Github/ml-latino-vote-2020")
raw_file<-file.path(source_root,"data/raw/39096-0001-Data.rda")
raw_md5<-unname(tools::md5sum(raw_file))
stopifnot(raw_md5=="a02f00860e598a49720a396c6f829873")
e<-new.env();load(raw_file,envir=e);raw<-e[["da39096.0001"]];rm(e)
stopifnot(identical(dim(raw),c(17545L,1490L)))
code<-function(x) {
 if(is.numeric(x))return(as.numeric(x))
 suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("^\\(([0-9]+)\\).*","\\1",as.character(x))))
}
clean_text<-function(x)trimws(iconv(x,from="",to="UTF-8",sub=""))
latino<-code(raw$MAIN_ETH_QUOTA)==2
primary_sample<-code(raw$BASELINE)==1
registered<-code(raw$S6)==1
voted<-code(raw$Q12)%in%1:2
candidate<-code(raw$Q14)
rows<-which(latino & primary_sample & registered & voted & candidate%in%1:5)
d<-raw[rows,,drop=FALSE];y<-as.integer(code(d$Q14)==1);w<-as.numeric(d$WEIGHT)
stopifnot(length(y)==2082L,all(is.finite(w)),all(w>0),!anyNA(y),!anyDuplicated(rows))
flow<-data.frame(stage=c("Raw records","Latino quota, all releases","Registered Latino, all releases",
 "Reported voters, all releases","Valid choice, all releases","Primary release, all races",
 "Primary Latino quota","Registered primary Latino","Reported primary Latino voters","Valid choice: final sample"),
 n=c(nrow(raw),sum(latino),sum(latino & registered),sum(latino & registered & voted),
 sum(latino & registered & voted & candidate%in%1:5),sum(primary_sample),sum(primary_sample & latino),
 sum(primary_sample & latino & registered),sum(primary_sample & latino & registered & voted),length(y)))
contract<-data.frame(n=length(y),trump=sum(y),unweighted_trump=mean(y),weighted_trump=weighted.mean(y,w),
 weight_min=min(w),weight_max=max(w),weight_kish_n=sum(w)^2/sum(w^2))
out<-"results";dir.create(out,showWarnings=FALSE)
write.csv(flow,file.path(out,"sample-flow.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(contract,file.path(out,"sample-summary.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
candidates<-data.frame(candidate=levels(d$Q14),n=as.integer(table(d$Q14)),
 weighted_share=as.numeric(tapply(w,d$Q14,sum)/sum(w)))
write.csv(candidates,file.path(out,"candidate-distribution.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
vars<-names(raw);labels<-attr(raw,"variable.labels")
label<-setNames(vapply(vars,function(n){a<-labels[n];if(is.na(a))n else clean_text(a)},character(1)),vars)

masked<-c("S3BR4OE","S3R4OE","S8_PACIFICR8OE","S8R16OE","S9R19OE","S10R22OE","S11R13OE","S12R27OE","S15",
 "Q259","Q426R1","Q426R2","Q427R1","Q427R2",paste0("Q471R",1:5),"Q772","Q776","Q777B","Q778R1","Q780R1",
 "Q781","Q783","Q784",paste0("Q786R",1:3),"Q787R1","Q789R1")

 "S6","S6_NON","Q12","Q14","S5_AGE","Q3B_PLURAL","ASIAN_ETH","MENA_MUSLIM","HAWAII_PI","LGBTQ","AFROLAT","BLACKIMM","NATIVEAM",
 "S10HOLD","Q58_COUNT","Q58SELECT","C2PID","C2PP","C3PID","C3PP","SCREENTIMESCM6T","QTIME","VOS","VBROWSER","VMOBILEDEVICE","VMOBILEOS")
is_survey<-grepl("^(S[0-9]|Q[0-9]|NEWQ[0-9]|VQ[0-9])",vars)
context<-rep(FALSE,length(vars)) # No appended census contextual fields in this release.
metadata<-grepl("SPLIT|_HID$|^RAND_|_TEXT$|TEXT$|^Q340_|^Q340(A|B)|^HOLDCOND|^NOANSWER",vars)
free_text<-grepl("OE$",vars) | vapply(raw,function(v)is.factor(v) &&
 !all(grepl("^\\([0-9]+\\)",levels(v),useBytes=TRUE)),logical(1)) & !vars%in%c("S4")
reason<-ifelse(is_survey,"Eligible","Not a source survey response; administration or derived metadata")
reason[metadata]<-"Routing/experiment metadata; joined to response where required"
reason[free_text]<-"Uncoded/free-text field; no text model"
reason[vars%in%admin]<-"Outcome, selection, administration, weights or duplicate"
reason[vars%in%masked]<-"ICPSR disclosure-masked field"
# Conceptual exclusions fixed before fitting; no importance-dependent exclusions.
qnum<-suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub("^Q([0-9]+).*","\\1",vars)))
proximate<-vars[(qnum%in%c(2,15,47:56,130,195:201,272,323:328,340:341,575,614:615,684)) |
 vars%in%c("Q96R10","Q96R11","Q96R12","Q98R8","Q98R9","Q504R11","Q504R12","Q509_Q511R3")]
partisan<-vars[qnum%in%c(17:19,21:28,294,301,315,334,743:745) |
 vars%in%c("Q1R17","Q1R18","Q225R10","Q225R11","Q287R6","Q316R7","Q560R4")]
proximate<-na.omit(proximate);partisan<-na.omit(partisan)
# Numeric ratings/ranks are categorical; continuous sliders and allocations retain magnitudes.
ordinal_numeric<-grep("^Q504R|^Q603R|^Q674R?",vars,value=TRUE)
continuous<-vars[vapply(raw,is.numeric,logical(1)) & !vars%in%ordinal_numeric & reason=="Eligible"]
continuous<-union(continuous,c("Q742","Q806","Q808"))
x<-d[,vars[reason=="Eligible"],drop=FALSE]
for(n in names(x)) {
 if(n%in%c("Q742","Q806","Q808"))x[[n]]<-suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("^\\([0-9]+\\) *","",as.character(x[[n]]))))
 else if(n%in%ordinal_numeric)x[[n]]<-ifelse(is.na(x[[n]]),NA_character_,as.character(x[[n]]))
 else if(is.factor(x[[n]]))x[[n]]<-clean_text(as.character(x[[n]]))
}
# Conditions are excluded as standalone predictors. Fields already separated by wording
# retain separate source codes, with condition text appended for explicit interpretation.
condition<-setNames(rep(list(character()),length(vars)),vars)
join_condition<-function(n,cond){for(v in intersect(n,names(x)))condition[[v]]<<-unique(c(condition[[v]],cond))}
join_condition(paste0("Q",48:50),"Q48_50SPLIT")
join_condition(paste0("Q",51:52),"Q51_52SPLIT")
join_condition(grep("^Q257[A-C]R",vars,value=TRUE),"Q257SPLIT")
join_condition("Q258","Q258SPLIT")
join_condition("Q272",c("RAND_POS1","RAND_POS2","RAND_SCORE1","RAND_SCORE2"))
join_condition(grep("^Q323_|^Q325_|^Q326R|^Q324$",vars,value=TRUE),"Q323BLWSPLIT")
join_condition(paste0("Q",347:349),"Q347SPLIT")
join_condition(paste0("Q",517:520),"SPLITA")
join_condition(grep("^Q693_Q700R",vars,value=TRUE),"SPLITQ693_Q700")
join_condition("Q715_718R2","SPLITQ716")
join_condition(grep("^Q607_Q610R",vars,value=TRUE),"Q607TEXT")
join_condition("Q340",grep("^Q340_",vars,value=TRUE))
join_condition("Q341R1",grep("^Q340_.*_1$",vars,value=TRUE))
join_condition("Q341R2",grep("^Q340_.*_2$",vars,value=TRUE))
# Piped identity targets vary even within the Latino quota.
for(n in names(x)[grepl("S2_Race_Prime",label[names(x)],fixed=TRUE)])join_condition(n,"S2_RACE_PRIME")
join_condition(c("Q287R6"),c("Q21","Q23"))
join_condition("Q22","Q21")
join_condition("Q744","Q743")
# Q315 wording is disputed; preserve supplied categories and join selected identity,
# while removing it entirely in Model 3 because the target can reveal party identity.
identity_target<-as.character(d$Q294)
identity_target[code(d$Q287SPLIT)==2]<-as.character(d$C2PID[code(d$Q287SPLIT)==2])
identity_target[code(d$Q287SPLIT)==3]<-as.character(d$C3PID[code(d$Q287SPLIT)==3])
if("Q315"%in%names(x))x$Q315<-paste(x$Q315,identity_target,sep=" | Selected identity: ")
for(n in names(x))if(length(condition[[n]])) {
 response<-as.character(x[[n]])
 cond<-vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)),function(i)paste(vapply(condition[[n]],function(cn){a<-clean_text(as.character(d[[cn]][i]));
  if(is.na(a))a<-"Condition not recorded";paste0(cn,": ",a)},character(1)),collapse=" | "),character(1))
 x[[n]]<-ifelse(is.na(response),NA_character_,paste(response,cond,sep=" | "))
}
# Group only components of one question (checkbox, ranking, constrained allocation).
# Distinct numbered questions in rating batteries remain separate questionnaire items.
grouped_prefixes<-c("Q32","Q39","Q41","Q60","Q76","Q110","Q116","Q281","Q355","Q366","Q465","Q471","Q475","Q490","Q491","Q512","Q534","Q550","Q659","Q662","Q750","Q751","Q793","Q794","Q796","Q826","S2_RACE","S2_HISPANIC","S2_NATIVE","S2_AFROLAT","Q1","Q27","Q28","Q30","Q31","Q38","Q58","Q61",
 "Q96","Q98","Q171","Q195A1","Q195A2","Q195B1","Q195B2","Q202","Q262","Q263","Q295","Q301","Q329","Q336",
 "Q407","Q428","Q539","Q603","Q606","Q629","Q797","Q798","Q799","Q800","Q801","Q802","Q807","Q815")
item_of<-function(n){if(grepl("^Q754_Q762R[0-9]+C[0-9]+$",n))return(sub("C[0-9]+$","",n));a<-sub("R[0-9]+(C[0-9]+)?$","",n);if(a%in%grouped_prefixes)a else n}
item_map<-setNames(vapply(names(x),item_of,character(1)),names(x))
ledger<-data.frame(variable=vars,item=vapply(vars,item_of,character(1)),verified_short_label=pretty_item(vars),
 construct=unname(label),wording_source="ICPSR variable label; may be truncated",codebook_pdf_page=unname(codebook_page[vars]),
 source_type=ifelse(is_survey,"Survey item or survey routing field","Administration / derived field"),appended_context=context,
 routing_notes=ifelse(vapply(condition,length,integer(1))>0,paste("Condition joined:",vapply(condition,paste,collapse="; ",character(1))),
 "Original questionnaire route / module retained; system NA not interpreted as a substantive answer"),
 missingness_type=ifelse(vars%in%masked,"Disclosure masked", "System NA: routing, nonresponse or unavailable; labelled responses preserved"),
 sample_system_missing=vapply(d,function(v)sum(is.na(v)),integer(1)),base_decision=reason,
 model1=reason=="Eligible",model2=reason=="Eligible" & !vars%in%proximate,
 model3=reason=="Eligible" & !vars%in%union(proximate,partisan),
```

```{r}
#| label: modeling-functions
#| include: false
auc_weighted <- function(y,p,w) {
 o<-order(p); y<-y[o]; p<-p[o]; w<-w[o]
 g<-cumsum(c(TRUE,diff(p)!=0)); pos<-as.numeric(rowsum(w*y,g)); neg<-as.numeric(rowsum(w*(1-y),g))
 sum(pos*(cumsum(neg)-neg/2))/(sum(pos)*sum(neg))
}
split_train <- function(y,seed,fraction=.75) {
 set.seed(seed)
 sort(unlist(lapply(split(seq_along(y),y),function(i)sample(i,floor(length(i)*fraction)))))
}
preprocess <- function(z,train,test) {
 a<-z[train,,drop=FALSE]; b<-z[test,,drop=FALSE]
 keep<-vapply(a,function(v)sum(!is.na(v))>=30 && mean(is.na(v))<=.9 &&
 length(unique(v[!is.na(v)]))>1,logical(1))
 a<-a[,keep,drop=FALSE];b<-b[,keep,drop=FALSE]
 aa<-bb<-list(); map<-character(); j<-0L
 add<-function(at,bt,item) {
  j<<-j+1L; key<-paste0("v",j)
  aa[[key]]<<-as.numeric(at);bb[[key]]<<-as.numeric(bt);map[key]<<-item
 }
 for(n in names(a)) {
  v<-a[[n]];q<-b[[n]];it<-item_map[[n]]
  if(is.character(v)||is.factor(v)) {
   v<-as.character(v);q<-as.character(q)
   v[is.na(v)]<-"Not observed / routed";q[is.na(q)]<-"Not observed / routed"
   tab<-table(v); good<-names(tab)[tab>=10]
   v[!v %in% good]<-"Rare / novel";q[!q %in% good]<-"Rare / novel"
   for(l in sort(unique(v))) add(v==l,q==l,it)
  } else {
   med<-median(v,na.rm=TRUE)
   add(ifelse(is.na(v),med,v),ifelse(is.na(q),med,q),it)
   if(anyNA(v)) add(is.na(v),is.na(q),it)
  }
 }
 aa<-as.data.frame(aa);bb<-as.data.frame(bb)
 keep<-vapply(aa,function(v)length(unique(v))>1,logical(1))
 aa<-aa[,keep,drop=FALSE];bb<-bb[,keep,drop=FALSE];map<-map[keep]
 stopifnot(ncol(aa)>0,identical(names(aa),names(bb)),!anyNA(aa),!anyNA(bb),
 all(is.finite(as.matrix(aa))),all(is.finite(as.matrix(bb))))
 list(train=aa,test=bb,map=map,retained=names(a))
}
rf_fit <- function(a,y,w,mtry_kind,node,trees,seed) {
 p<-ncol(a)
 mtry<-switch(mtry_kind,
  sqrt=floor(sqrt(p)),
  fraction20=floor(0.20*p),
  fraction40=floor(0.40*p),
  stop("Unknown mtry option: ",mtry_kind))
 ranger::ranger(x=a,y=factor(y,levels=0:1),probability=TRUE,num.trees=trees,
 mtry=max(1L,mtry),min.node.size=node,case.weights=w/mean(w),
 num.threads=2,seed=seed,write.forest=TRUE)
}
rf_predict <- function(f,a) predict(f,data=a,num.threads=2)$predictions[,"1"]
metrics <- function(y,p,w,reference) {
 p<-pmin(pmax(p,1e-6),1-1e-6);lp<-qlogis(p)
 cal<-suppressWarnings(glm(y~lp,weights=w/mean(w),family=quasibinomial()))
 intercept<-suppressWarnings(glm(y~1,offset=lp,weights=w/mean(w),family=quasibinomial()))
 data.frame(n=length(y),trump=sum(y),prevalence=weighted.mean(y,w),
 auc=auc_weighted(y,p,w),brier=weighted.mean((y-p)^2,w),
 reference_brier=weighted.mean((y-reference)^2,w),mean_prediction=weighted.mean(p,w),
 calibration_intercept=unname(coef(intercept)[1]),calibration_slope=unname(coef(cal)[2]))
}
cal_bins <- function(y,p,w) {
 bin<-cut(p,breaks=seq(0,1,.2),include.lowest=TRUE)
 do.call(rbind,lapply(levels(bin),function(k){i<-which(bin==k);if(length(i)<10)return(NULL)
 data.frame(bin=k,n=length(i),mean_prediction=weighted.mean(p[i],w[i]),
 observed_share=weighted.mean(y[i],w[i]))}))
}
explain_aggregate <- function(f,prep,z,test,w,seed) {
 ref<-prep$train
 u<-treeshap::ranger.unify(f,ref)
 sh<-as.matrix(treeshap::treeshap(u,prep$test,verbose=FALSE)$shaps)
 p<-rf_predict(f,prep$test);base<-mean(rf_predict(f,ref))
 error<-max(abs(base+rowSums(sh)-p));
 message("SHAP reconstruction maximum error=",error)
 stopifnot(error<1e-6)
 grouped<-t(rowsum(t(sh),group=prep$map,reorder=FALSE))
 imp<-colSums(abs(grouped)*w$test)/sum(w$test)
 global<-data.frame(item=names(imp),importance=as.numeric(imp),row.names=NULL)
 global$rank<-rank(-global$importance,ties.method="min")
 # Save aggregate directional cells for every retained source variable, not individual scores.
 direction<-list()
 for(n in prep$retained) {
  it<-item_map[[n]];if(!it %in% colnames(grouped))next
  v<-z[[n]][test]
  if(is.numeric(v)&&length(unique(v[!is.na(v)]))>12) {
   breaks<-unique(quantile(z[[n]][attr(z,"train")],c(0,.25,.5,.75,1),na.rm=TRUE))
   if(length(breaks)>2){breaks[c(1,length(breaks))]<-c(-Inf,Inf);v<-as.character(cut(v,breaks,include.lowest=TRUE))}
  }
  v<-as.character(v);v[is.na(v)]<-"Not observed / routed"
  direction[[n]]<-do.call(rbind,lapply(sort(unique(v)),function(l){i<-which(v==l);if(length(i)<10)return(NULL)
   data.frame(item=it,variable=n,response=l,n=length(i),weight_sum=sum(w$test[i]),
   mean_shap=weighted.mean(grouped[i,it],w$test[i]),
   positive_share=weighted.mean(grouped[i,it]>0,w$test[i]),row.names=NULL)
  }))
 }
 list(importance=global[order(global$rank),],direction=do.call(rbind,direction),
 additivity_error=error,baseline=base)
}
run_development <- function(spec,seed) {
 message("Starting ",spec," ",seed)
 train_all<-split_train(y,seed);test_all<-setdiff(seq_along(y),train_all)
 use<-seq_along(y)
 train<-intersect(train_all,use);test<-intersect(test_all,use)
 eligible<-switch(spec,diagnostic=names(x),primary=setdiff(names(x),proximate),
 withheld=setdiff(names(x),union(proximate,partisan)))
 z<-x[,eligible,drop=FALSE];attr(z,"train")<-train
 inner<-split_train(y[train],seed+11,.8);it<-train[inner];iv<-train[-inner]
 tuning_pre<-preprocess(z,it,iv)
 grid<-expand.grid(mtry=c("sqrt","fraction20","fraction40"),node=c(5L,20L,50L),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
 {
  scores<-vapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)),function(k){
   f<-rf_fit(tuning_pre$train,y[it],w[it],grid$mtry[k],grid$node[k],150L,seed+20)
   p<-rf_predict(f,tuning_pre$test);weighted.mean((y[iv]-p)^2,w[iv])},numeric(1))
  tuning<-cbind(grid,encoded_p=ncol(tuning_pre$train),
   actual_mtry=vapply(grid$mtry,function(k)switch(k,sqrt=floor(sqrt(ncol(tuning_pre$train))),
    fraction20=floor(.20*ncol(tuning_pre$train)),fraction40=floor(.40*ncol(tuning_pre$train)),
    stop("Unknown mtry option")),numeric(1)),validation_brier=scores);best<-which.min(scores)
  prep<-preprocess(z,train,test)
  fit<-rf_fit(prep$train,y[train],w[train],grid$mtry[best],grid$node[best],300L,seed+30)
  pred<-rf_predict(fit,prep$test)
  agg<-explain_aggregate(fit,prep,z,test,list(train=w[train],test=w[test]),seed+40)
 }
 score<-metrics(y[test],pred,w[test],weighted.mean(y[train],w[train]))
 score$n_train<-length(train);score$encoded_columns<-ncol(prep$train)
 score$items<-length(unique(prep$map));score$seed<-seed;score$spec<-spec
 score$learner<-"forest";score$population<-"All voters"
 list(metrics=score,calibration=cal_bins(y[test],pred,w[test]),tuning=tuning,
 chosen=tuning[best,,drop=FALSE],importance=agg$importance,direction=agg$direction,
 additivity_error=agg$additivity_error,baseline=agg$baseline,
 retained_variables=prep$retained,feature_map=data.frame(encoded=names(prep$map),item=unname(prep$map)))
}
```

```{r}
 ((tp[i]>tp[negative])+.5*(tp[i]==tp[negative]))),numeric(1)))/(sum(tw[positive])*sum(tw[negative]))
stopifnot(abs(auc_weighted(ty,tp,tw)-manual_auc)<1e-12,
```

```{r}
cfg<-list(seeds=202001:202003,trees=300L,tune_trees=150L,reference="complete unweighted training sample",
 rare_n=10L,min_observed=30L,max_missing=.9,mtry_grid=c("sqrt","fraction20","fraction40"),node_grid=c(5L,20L,50L),version="frozen-grid-2020-primary-v1")
functions_for_hash<-list(auc_weighted,split_train,preprocess,rf_fit,rf_predict,metrics,cal_bins,
 explain_aggregate,run_development)
# Hash function text, not R source references or execution environments.
functions_for_hash<-lapply(functions_for_hash,function(f)list(formals=deparse(formals(f)),body=deparse(body(f))))
key<-digest::digest(list(cfg,raw_md5,functions_for_hash,digest::digest(x),names(x),item_map,condition,
 proximate,partisan,continuous,R.version.string,
 vapply(c("ranger","treeshap"),function(p)as.character(packageVersion(p)),character(1))))
result_dir<-file.path(out,"fits");dir.create(result_dir,showWarnings=FALSE)
# Optional scratch storage supports layout-only rerenders; no permanent fit cache.
 scratch<-Sys.getenv("CMPS2020_SCRATCH",tempfile("cmps2020-"))
 dir.create(scratch,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
 objects<-c("raw_md5","rows","y","w","x","proximate","partisan","continuous","condition","item_map")
 fun<-c("code","clean_text","auc_weighted","split_train","preprocess","rf_predict","metrics","cal_bins","explain_aggregate")
 hashes<-data.frame(component=c(objects,fun),hash=c(vapply(objects,function(n)digest::digest(get(n)),character(1)),
  vapply(fun,function(n){f<-get(n);digest::digest(list(formals=deparse(formals(f)),body=deparse(body(f))))},character(1))))
 write.csv(hashes,file.path(out,"computation-component-hashes.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
 # Explicit fitting-option contract, including rejection of unknown values.
 stopifnot(inherits(try(rf_fit(data.frame(a=1:4),c(0,1,0,1),rep(1,4),"unknown",5L,1L,1L),silent=TRUE),"try-error"))

{
 jobs<-expand.grid(spec=c("diagnostic","primary","withheld"),seed=cfg$seeds,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
 jobs$learner<-"forest";jobs$two_party<-FALSE
 results<-list()
 for(j in seq_len(nrow(jobs))) {
  job<-jobs[j,];name<-paste(job$spec,job$seed,job$learner,job$two_party,sep="_")
  file<-file.path(scratch,paste0(name,".rds"))
  old<-if(file.exists(file))readRDS(file) else NULL
  if(!is.null(old)&&identical(old$key,key)){results[[name]]<-old$result;next}
  ans<-run_development(job$spec,job$seed)
  stopifnot(is.null(ans$model),is.null(ans$predictions),is.null(ans$signed_shap),
   is.null(ans$row_id),is.null(ans$train_idx),is.null(ans$test_idx),
   is.null(ans$direction)||all(ans$direction$n>=10))
  saveRDS(list(key=key,result=ans),file)
  results[[name]]<-ans
  message("Completed ",name,": AUC=",round(ans$metrics$auc,3)," Brier=",round(ans$metrics$brier,3))
 }
 performance<-do.call(rbind,lapply(results,`[[`,"metrics"));rownames(performance)<-NULL
 write.csv(performance,file.path(result_dir,"performance.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
 bind_tagged<-function(field) {
  pieces<-lapply(names(results),function(n){z<-results[[n]][[field]]
   if(is.null(z)||!nrow(z))return(NULL);cbind(run=n,z)})
  pieces<-Filter(Negate(is.null),pieces)
  cols<-unique(unlist(lapply(pieces,names)))
  do.call(rbind,lapply(pieces,function(z){for(n in setdiff(cols,names(z)))z[[n]]<-NA;z[,cols,drop=FALSE]}))
 }
 for(field in c("importance","direction","calibration","tuning"))
  write.csv(bind_tagged(field),file.path(result_dir,paste0(field,".csv")),row.names=FALSE)
 # Ranks and importance are conditional on retention; absent fits are recorded separately below.
 imp<-bind_tagged("importance")
 imp$spec<-sub("_[0-9].*","",imp$run)
 imp$population<-ifelse(grepl("TRUE$",imp$run),"Two-party","All voters")
 stability<-do.call(rbind,lapply(split(imp,interaction(imp$spec,imp$population,drop=TRUE)),function(z)
  do.call(rbind,lapply(split(z,z$item),function(a)data.frame(spec=a$spec[1],population=a$population[1],
  item=a$item[1],retained_refits=nrow(a),rank_mean=mean(a$rank),
  rank_min=min(a$rank),rank_median=median(a$rank),rank_max=max(a$rank),
  importance_mean=mean(a$importance),importance_min=min(a$importance),importance_max=max(a$importance))))))
 write.csv(stability,file.path(result_dir,"stability.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
 writeLines(c(paste("Computation fingerprint:",key),capture.output(dput(cfg)),
  paste("Source:",normalizePath(raw_file)),paste("Raw MD5:",raw_md5)),file.path(out,"run-manifest.txt"))
 writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()),file.path(out,"session-info.txt"))
}
```


# Sample and outcome

The sample comprises **2,082 Latino registered respondents in the primary release**
who reported voting and named a valid presidential choice. It includes
**`r sum(y)` Trump voters**: **`r sprintf("%.2f%%",100*mean(y))`** unweighted and **`r sprintf("%.2f%%",100*weighted.mean(y,w))`** weighted.
The other reported choices are Biden, Jorgensen, Hawkins, or someone else.
Respondents who answered a nonvoter candidate-support version are excluded.

$$Y_i=\begin{cases}1&\text{Trump vote}\\0&\text{other reported presidential vote}\end{cases}$$

The within-racial-group **WEIGHT** targets the 2019 ACS adult population using
age, gender, education, nativity, and ancestry margins. The primary-sample
methodology recommends this weight for multivariate analysis. It is applied to
the voter subset without trimming or class balancing; it is not a separate
calibration to Latino voters. The primary-release restriction excludes 138
otherwise eligible quota-group voters whose weight scope is not established by
that documentation. Exact definitions and release discrepancies appear in the audit.

# Three nested models

| Model | Information available | Purpose |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1. Full | All otherwise eligible survey responses | Describe the full predictive structure |
| 2. Outcome-proximate withheld | Model 1 minus candidate and election-proximate responses | Describe differentiation beyond information close to vote choice |
| 3. Direct partisanship withheld | Model 2 minus direct partisan information; ideology retained | Describe differentiation beyond explicit partisan attachment |

Model 2 withholds candidate evaluations, congressional vote, presidential-election
fraud and January 6 reactions, candidate-framed anxiety and policy evaluations,
and hypothetical candidate-response experiments. Model 3 additionally withholds
party identification, strength, leaning, history, party associations and affinity,
party-selected identity responses, partisan redistricting tradeoffs, and spouse's
partisanship. Generic political activity and policy attitudes remain eligible.
No exclusion depends on an item's fitted importance.

# Why random forest + SHAP

The random forest estimates $\hat p_i=f(X_i)$ and allows nonlinear relationships
and interactions without specifying their forms beforehand. TreeSHAP decomposes
its predictions relative to a training reference:

$$\hat p_i\approx\phi_0+\sum_j\phi_{ij}.$$

Weighted mean absolute SHAP, $I_j=E_w(|\phi_{ij}|)$, measures an item's overall
predictive contribution. Contributions from encoded columns are summed back to
the original item **before** taking absolute values. Signed SHAP describes
responses associated with predictions above or below the model reference.
Neither is a causal effect. Correlated items can share or substitute for one
another's predictive contributions.

The complete outer training sample supplies the unweighted TreeSHAP reference
for tree-path frequencies. Survey weights enter forest resampling, evaluation,
global importance, and response-level summaries. No individual predictions or
individual SHAP arrays are exported.

# Validation and stability

Three outcome-stratified 75/25 outer splits use seeds **202001, 202002, 202003**.
Each outer training portion has an 80/20 internal training/validation split.
Nine candidates cross $\lfloor\sqrt p\rfloor$, $\lfloor0.20p\rfloor$, and
$\lfloor0.40p\rfloor$ with node sizes 5, 20, and 50; $p$ is the encoded feature
count after the relevant training-only preprocessing. Weighted validation Brier
loss selects a setting using 150 trees; the final forest uses 300 trees.
The grid is frozen even when 40% is selected.

All screening and preprocessing use only the relevant training portion: at least
30 observed responses, at most 90% system missingness, variation checks,
category pooling below 10 training cases, numeric median imputation, and removal
of constant encoded columns. Numeric missingness indicators belong to their
source item. Categorical system missingness has an explicit “Not observed /
routed” category. Original labelled responses—including don't know, refused,
none, and unfamiliar—remain distinct unless pooled by the training rule.
There is no blanket deletion of numeric codes and no reverse scoring.

Randomized wording is joined to the relevant answer. Rating categories retain
original orientation; numeric opinion scales and ranks are not automatically
continuous. Continuous sliders, point allocations, birth year, and verified
calendar-year quantities retain their magnitudes. Signed summaries use original
responses, with at least 10 holdout observations per cell. Continuous measures
with more than 12 distinct values use training-derived quartile bins.

The holdouts never select predictors, transformations, or tuning settings. They
overlap across fits: these are stability checks, not independent replications,
and ranges are **not confidence intervals**. Calibration is diagnostic; fitted
probabilities are not presented as individual political scores.

```{r}
#| label: research-summaries
#| include: false
names_pretty<-c(diagnostic="Model 1: Full",primary="Model 2: Outcome-proximate withheld", withheld="Model 3: Direct partisanship withheld")
fmt<-function(z,digits=3)paste0(formatC(mean(z),digits=digits,format="f")," [",
 formatC(min(z),digits=digits,format="f"),", ",formatC(max(z),digits=digits,format="f"),"]")
summary_table<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(names_pretty),function(s){z<-performance[performance$spec==s,]
 data.frame(Model=paste("Model",match(s,names(names_pretty))),AUC=fmt(z$auc),Brier=fmt(z$brier),Reference=fmt(z$reference_brier))}))
write.csv(summary_table,file.path(out,"performance-summary.csv"),row.names=FALSE)

response_expansions<-data.frame(variable=c("Q543","Q543","Q614","Q614","Q2R1","Q24","Q25"),
 code=c(1,2,1,2,6,88,88),
 response=c("Support government increasing spending by $25 billion on border security, including building a wall between the U.S. and Mexico",
 "Oppose government increasing spending by $25 billion on border security, including building a wall between the U.S. and Mexico",
 "I oppose Trump's immigration policies","I support Trump's immigration policies","Haven't heard enough to say","Don't know","Don't know"),
 questionnaire_pdf_page=c(94,94,101,101,13,15,15))
write.csv(response_expansions,file.path(out,"response-label-expansions.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
response_display<-function(v,r){rr<-r
 for(i in seq_along(r)){hit<-which(response_expansions$variable==v & response_expansions$code==code(r[i]));
 if(length(hit)==1)rr[i]<-paste0("(",code(r[i]),") ",response_expansions$response[hit])};rr}

dirs<-bind_tagged("direction");dirs$spec<-sub("_[0-9].*","",dirs$run)
groups<-split(seq_len(nrow(dirs)),paste(dirs$spec,dirs$variable,dirs$response,sep="\r"))

 refits=nrow(a),n_min=min(a$n),n_max=max(a$n),mean_shap=mean(a$mean_shap),
 minimum=min(a$mean_shap),maximum=max(a$mean_shap),positive_refits=sum(a$mean_shap>0),
 negative_refits=sum(a$mean_shap<0),row.names=NULL)}))
write.csv(directional_stability,file.path(out,"directional-stability.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
profiles<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(names_pretty),function(s){z<-stability[stability$spec==s,]
 z<-z[order(-z$importance_mean,z$item),];z$ordered_position<-seq_len(nrow(z))
 z$adjacent_gap<-z$importance_mean-c(z$importance_mean[-1],NA_real_);z}))
profiles$label<-pretty_item(profiles$item)
write.csv(profiles,file.path(out,"importance-profile-all-items.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
# Complete eligible item-by-fit grid: absent fitted items are NA, never silent zeroes.
all_ranks<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(results),function(n){a<-results[[n]];s<-a$metrics$spec
 eligible<-switch(s,diagnostic=names(x),primary=setdiff(names(x),proximate),
  withheld=setdiff(names(x),union(proximate,partisan)))
 g<-data.frame(item=unique(unname(item_map[eligible])))
 g<-merge(g,a$importance,by="item",all.x=TRUE,sort=FALSE)

plot_profile<-function(s) {

  Range=paste(z$rank_min,z$rank_max,sep="–"),Fits=z$retained_refits,

 knitr::asis_output(sub("\\midrule","\\midrule\n\\endhead",as.character(tab),fixed=TRUE))
}
dir.create(file.path(out,"figures"),showWarnings=FALSE)
for(s in names(names_pretty)) {
```

# 2020 results

Performance is reported as mean [minimum, maximum] across three weighted outer
holdouts. Smaller Brier loss indicates smaller prediction error. The reference
Brier uses the outer-training weighted Trump prevalence.

```{r}
knitr::kable(summary_table,row.names=FALSE)
```

## Model 1 — Full

Congressional vote, Trump immigration-policy approval, and Trump favorability
rank first, second, and third in every split. Their mean absolute contributions
are 15.44, 6.56, and 4.23 percentage points. Trump responsibility for COVID-19 and
January 6, other candidate evaluations, and hypothetical presidential choices
follow. This strong predictive separation relies heavily on information close
to the reported electoral choice.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.5

plot_profile("diagnostic")
```

```{r}
model_table("diagnostic")
```

## Model 2 — Outcome-proximate measures withheld

Party identification and Republican and Democratic party histories occupy the
first three positions in mean importance, although their individual ranks vary.
Border-security spending and issue priorities follow. Associations of groups
with the two parties become especially prominent in one split, so a fixed order
among partisan measures is not stable. BLM support, BLM warmth, and the
most-disliked-group ranking also remain prominent. Routed party histories repeat
information about attachment and should not be interpreted as independent
partisan mechanisms.


## Model 3 — Direct partisanship withheld

Border-security spending and BLM support rank first and second in every split,
with mean absolute contributions of 7.41 and 5.00 percentage points. The
most-disliked-group ranking, issue priorities, and BLM warmth occupy positions
3–5 in each fit. Ideology follows at ranks 6–7. Racial bias in policing and
immigration enforcement, gun-owner warmth, and the border-priority tradeoff are
also recurrent. These responses describe differentiation beyond explicit party
attachment; they are not necessarily independent of partisanship.

# How the prominent items behave

## Importance and stability

The three tables show the first 30 positions. All-item outputs include each fit's
importance and rank, across-fit means and ranges, number of fits retained, and
the adjacent mean-importance gap $\Delta_k=I_k-I_{k+1}$. Means weight fits equally
after weighting within each holdout; item means are conditional on retention.
The complete eligible item-by-fit grid records nonretention as missing, not zero.
Gaps are descriptive, not significance tests. The top-50 profiles show the shape
of the distribution without selecting a final substantive threshold.

The sharpest stable ordering is at the top of Models 1 and 3. Below these leading
positions, rank ranges often widen. In Model 2, party identification ranges from
rank 1 to 3, but Democratic-group associations range from 1 to 15 and party
leaning from 11 to 112. This variation cautions against treating small differences
in average rank as fixed substantive distinctions. All displayed items are
retained in all three fits; the complete output also records less consistently
retained items.

## Signed responses and nonlinear patterns

Positive signed SHAP moves a fitted prediction toward Trump vote relative to the
reference; negative values move it away. Each response mean is weighted within
fit, then averaged across fits. Tables require at least 10 holdout observations
in each of all three fits. “N per fit” gives the observed range; the saved
`direction.csv` records the count separately for each fit. For grouped questions,
a component response conditions the whole item's contribution, not an isolated
component effect. Response labels below preserve the supplied categories;
verified expansions of truncated labels are documented separately.

```{r}
#| label: signed-patterns
#| results: asis
selections<-list(diagnostic=c("Q15","Q614","Q2R1"),primary=c("Q21"),withheld=c("Q543","Q358","Q43","Q606R1","Q606R3"))
for(s in names(selections))for(it in selections[[s]]) {
 z<-directional_stability[directional_stability$spec==s &
 directional_stability$variable==it & directional_stability$refits==3,]
 if(!nrow(z))next
 if(all(grepl("^[0-9]+$",z$response)))z<-z[order(as.numeric(z$response)),]
 cat("\n\n### ",names_pretty[[s]]," — ",pretty_item(it)," (",it,")\n\n",sep="")
 print(knitr::kable(data.frame(Response=sub("^\\([0-9]+\\) *","",response_display(it,z$response)),
 `SHAP (pp)`=round(100*z$mean_shap,2),
 `Range (pp)`=paste(round(100*z$minimum,2),round(100*z$maximum,2),sep=" to "),
 `N per fit`=paste(z$n_min,z$n_max,sep="–"),check.names=FALSE),
 format="latex",booktabs=TRUE,longtable=TRUE,align=c("p{3.05in}","r","r","r"),row.names=FALSE))
 cat("\n\n")
}
```

The signed patterns refine the interpretation of importance. In Model 1,
Trump favorability is roughly ordered, but even “somewhat unfavorable” has a
positive contribution relative to the reference; “very unfavorable” is the
consistently negative category. The item should not be reduced to a favorable
versus unfavorable contrast. Trump immigration-policy opposition and support
have consistently opposite signs, as do Democratic and Republican congressional
votes.

In Model 2, Republican identification contributes positively and Democratic
identification negatively in every fit. Independent and other-party means change
sign across fits and are much closer to zero.

In Model 3, support for the specified border-security spending and wall is
positive in every fit; opposition is negative. BLM support shows an
**extreme-category pattern**, not a smooth support-to-opposition gradient:
strong opposition contributes +11.81 percentage points on average [10.30, 13.86],
whereas somewhat opposing averages +0.58 [−1.01, 1.85], with an unstable sign.
Strong support, somewhat support, and neither support nor oppose all have
negative means. The same strong-opposition distinction appears in Model 2
(+3.18 [2.20, 3.82]); somewhat opposing is near zero and unstable there too.

Very conservative ideology contributes much more positively than somewhat
conservative ideology; liberal and moderate responses are negative. This is a
broad directional pattern with a pronounced conservative endpoint, rather than
equal steps across an ordinal scale.

The most-disliked-group ranking is also differentiated: placing White
supremacists first is associated with a negative whole-item contribution, while
placing them second or third is positive. Ranking BLM activists among the three
most disliked groups is positive in every displayed rank. These are conditional
summaries of the complete ranking, not separate effects of moving a group.

Selecting border security as an issue priority (`Q1R19`) accompanies a +9.71
percentage-point mean for the **whole priority item** [4.70, 12.92; 80–83 cases
per fit], versus −1.78 [−2.25, −0.88; 438–441 cases] when not selected. This is
not an isolated contribution of that checkbox. On anxiety from White supremacy
(`Q504R6`, 1 = least, 10 = most), the lowest category contributes +0.94
[0.56, 1.37; 69–84 cases], while categories 2 and 4 have means near zero with
unstable signs. A simple linear anxiety interpretation is not supported.
Continuous warmth measures have training-specific quartile boundaries; their
saved signed cells should be compared only when the intervals match.

# What is fixed for the later election analysis

The later 2024 analysis preserves reported vote rather than nonvoter support,
within-group weighting, the three nested information sets, training-only
preprocessing, the frozen nine-setting grid, repeated holdout assessment,
item-level SHAP, and signed response interpretation. Sample definitions, survey
weights, wording, routing, and variable exclusions require fresh wave-specific
audits. No cross-election harmonization, comparison, or final importance cutoff
is established here.

# Technical audit / reproducibility notes

## Sources and sample construction

The source data are `39096-0001-Data.rda`, object `da39096.0001`, with 17,545 rows
and 1,490 variables. The local questionnaire and ICPSR codebook are
`39096-Questionnaire.pdf` and `39096-0001-Codebook-ICPSR.pdf`.
Exact paths, roles, MD5 and SHA-256 checksums are in `source-manifest.csv`.
The earlier preparation and analysis files were inspected as context but are not
sourced or used as a prepared dataset. The QMD contains all executable preparation,
fitting, aggregation, and reporting functions.

Questionnaire PDF pp. 5 and 13 (printed pp. 3 and 11) establish registration and vote routing:
`S6=1`, `Q12=1` (“certain I voted”) or `Q12=2` (“think I voted”), and `Q14=1:5`.
Trump is `Q14=1`; Biden is 2, Jorgensen 3, Hawkins 4, someone else 5. Nonvoters
receive support wording in the same source field and are excluded by the turnout
condition. Voting mode (`Q13`) is asked only of certain voters; its structural
missingness remains explicit. Latino membership uses `MAIN_ETH_QUOTA=2`, not an
assumption that every Hispanic-ancestry response identifies the same sample.

`BASELINE=1` restricts the run to the primary release. This resolves the weight
scope choice explicitly before fitting. The raw field is labelled “Sept 1 2021
release”; it is the available primary-release indicator, not a claim that the
public-use extract exactly reproduces the published primary sample.

```{r}
knitr::kable(flow,row.names=FALSE)
```

The [official primary-sample methodology](https://ucla.box.com/shared/static/v11w0d769vvpu2skia9fym12q34ef4rj.pdf),
linked from the [CMPS 2020 survey page](https://cmps.ss.ucla.edu/2020-survey/), reports
14,988 primary interviews and 4,006 Latinos. The local primary indicator identifies
14,977 records, including 3,942 Latino-quota records (3,951 with `RACE=2`). These
counts differ from the publication and from each other; no cases are added or
reassigned to match published totals. The precise origin of the discrepancy
remains unresolved. The primary methodology describes April 2–August 25, 2021
fieldwork, after the election and January 6 events.

The methodology's pp. 1–2 specify within-racial-group raking to 2019 ACS one-year
adult margins for age, gender, education, nativity, and ancestry, within plus or
minus two percentage points, and recommend the weight for multivariate analysis.
The codebook labels `WEIGHT` “Primary sample weights ONLY”; `OS_WEIGHT` is an
oversample weight. The latter is not substituted for this primary-only run.
Weighting adults does not separately calibrate the selected registered voters.

## Wave-specific exclusion and routing rules

The ledger covers every source variable before any fit, including masked,
administrative, routing, and otherwise eligible fields. Common exclusions remove
the outcome and selection fields, identifiers, dates, weights, release flags,
uncoded/open text, masked fields, duplicate age categories, and routing-only
metadata. No appended census-context fields are identified in this extract.
Every remaining field is screened separately on the appropriate training data.

The following lists give eligible source fields removed at each step. Detailed
reasons and codebook PDF pages remain in the ledger.

```{r}
#| results: asis
for(k in c("Outcome-proximate","Direct partisan")) {
 v<-if(k=="Outcome-proximate")intersect(names(x),proximate) else setdiff(intersect(names(x),partisan),proximate)
 cat("\n\n**",k,"**: ",paste(paste0("`",v,"`"),collapse=", "),".\n\n",sep="")
}
```

Election-fraud and January 6 items are withheld as explicitly election-framed
responses, including news awareness (`Q47`) and the 2020 election tradeoff
(`Q684`). General voting rules, political participation, nonspecific campaign
contact, and electoral-college policy remain eligible. Candidate experiments
include ranked/single-choice 2024 vignettes (`Q195`–`Q201`), state-assembly choice
(`Q272`), candidate representation/trust (`Q323`–`Q328`), and the council conjoint
(`Q340`–`Q341`). The candidate-feeling battery `Q575_Q581` is withheld in full.
Generic desired representative traits remain eligible except explicit shared-party
preference. These are conceptual rules fixed before importance estimation.

The additional partisan exclusions include `Q17`–`Q19` foreign-party attachment
and its routed follow-ups; `Q21`–`Q28` identity/history and party associations;
party-antagonism priorities `Q1R17/R18`; party support/threat to one's vision of society `Q225R10/R11`;
party identity in `Q287R6`, `Q294`, `Q301`, `Q315`, `Q560R4`;
shared-party candidate preference `Q316R7`; partisan redistricting tradeoff
`Q334`; and spouse's identity/strength/leaning `Q743`–`Q745`.
The entire 100-point `Q301` allocation is withheld because its remaining components
could reconstruct the party allocation. Ideology (`Q43`) remains available. The least-liked-group ranking includes
Democratic Socialists and the Tea Party as named movements, not Democratic or
Republican party identification. It and its piped follow-ups remain eligible, as
do congressional-caucus evaluations and nonspecific campaign contact; these
boundary decisions do not claim that the responses are unrelated to partisanship.
No identifiable parental-party item was found. Racial, policy, religious,
economic, and demographic opinions are not removed merely as party proxies.

Randomized target/wording fields are joined where needed, including immigrant
health frames, representation vignettes, local-institution diversity, women’s
stereotypes, government-level trust, and outsider/insider wording. Distinct source
fields already tied to different wording remain distinct. The least-liked-group
pipe is joined to `Q607_Q610` responses. Rich conjoint profiles can produce rare
joint categories; the unchanged rare-level rule may remove their encoded variation.
Their policy eligibility does not guarantee retention. Placement-only metadata
never enters as a separate predictor.

## Measurement issues requiring review

ICPSR processing notes on codebook PDF p. 3 identify inconsistent wording for
`Q315` and `Q603R2` between the questionnaire and data. Supplied response labels
are retained; those codes receive review flags and no confident substantive name.
`Q315` is joined to its selected identity target and withheld from Model 3 because
that target can reveal party identity. `Q603R2` remains a component of the
source-learning ranking question; its disputed target must not be interpreted
as established. Truncated labels elsewhere remain linked to their source code
and are flagged where full wording has not been verified. The response-level
CSV preserves supplied category labels rather than guessing their completion.
Source codes and questionnaire numbers differ in places: data `Q614` is
questionnaire item 613 on Trump immigration policies; data `Q615` is item 614
on expressing that view. The verified crosswalk records these correspondences
by wording, including the shifted discrimination battery.

Calendar-year factors `Q742`, `Q806`, and `Q808` use their displayed years rather
than stored level indices. Birth year, sliders and allocations remain numeric;
`Q504`, `Q603`, and `Q674` rating/rank categories remain categorical. Explicit
special responses on other fields are not deleted. Duration fields retain their
supplied categories, including “less than a year.” System missingness cannot
distinguish every reason for nonresponse. Rare pooling may combine substantively
meaningful categories; `rare-category-training-audit.csv` records the affected
inner- and outer-training categories and counts.

## Fitted-feature and reconstruction audit

```{r}
#| label: final-audit
#| include: false
stopifnot(length(results)==9L)
feature_checks<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(results),function(n){a<-results[[n]];s<-a$metrics$spec
 blocked<-c(admin,vars[metadata|free_text],if(s!="diagnostic")proximate,
  if(s=="withheld")partisan)
 violations<-intersect(a$retained_variables,blocked)
 # Routing metadata can share an item prefix with an eligible response; do not
 # mistake that shared prefix for a fitted metadata column.
 allowed_items<-unique(vapply(a$retained_variables,item_of,character(1)))
 encoded_violations<-setdiff(a$feature_map$item,allowed_items)
 stopifnot(all(a$feature_map$item %in% vapply(a$retained_variables,item_of,character(1))))
 stopifnot(length(violations)==0,length(encoded_violations)==0,
  "Q43" %in% a$retained_variables,"Q43" %in% a$feature_map$item,
  !any(c("model","predictions","signed_shap","row_id","train_idx","test_idx") %in% names(a)),
  all(a$direction$n>=10))
 data.frame(run=n,retained_variables=length(a$retained_variables),
  encoded_columns=nrow(a$feature_map),excluded_variables_present=length(violations),
  excluded_encoded_items_present=length(encoded_violations),ideology_retained=TRUE,
  shap_max_error=a$additivity_error,mtry=a$chosen$mtry,node=a$chosen$node,
  outer_mtry=switch(a$chosen$mtry,sqrt=floor(sqrt(nrow(a$feature_map))),
   fraction20=floor(.2*nrow(a$feature_map)),fraction40=floor(.4*nrow(a$feature_map)),stop("Unknown mtry option")),
  inner_mtry=a$chosen$actual_mtry,inner_encoded_p=a$chosen$encoded_p)
}))
for(seed in cfg$seeds) {
 a<-lapply(names(names_pretty),function(s)results[[paste(s,seed,"forest_FALSE",sep="_")]])
 stopifnot(all(a[[2]]$retained_variables %in% a[[1]]$retained_variables),
  all(a[[3]]$retained_variables %in% a[[2]]$retained_variables),
  all(a[[2]]$feature_map$item %in% a[[1]]$feature_map$item),
  all(a[[3]]$feature_map$item %in% a[[2]]$feature_map$item))
}
stopifnot(max(feature_checks$shap_max_error)<1e-6)
write.csv(feature_checks,file.path(out,"fitted-feature-audit.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
retained_features<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(results),function(n)
 data.frame(run=n,variable=results[[n]]$retained_variables)))
write.csv(retained_features,file.path(out,"retained-source-variables.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
encoded_maps<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(results),function(n)
 data.frame(run=n,results[[n]]$feature_map)))
write.csv(encoded_maps,file.path(out,"encoded-item-maps.csv"),row.names=FALSE)

screening<-list()
for(seed in cfg$seeds){tr<-split_train(y,seed);inn<-tr[split_train(y[tr],seed+11,.8)]
 for(stage in c("inner","outer")){ii<-if(stage=="inner")inn else tr
 for(v in names(x)){a<-x[[v]][ii];obs<-sum(!is.na(a));missing<-mean(is.na(a));vary<-length(unique(a[!is.na(a)]))
 screening[[length(screening)+1L]]<-data.frame(seed=seed,stage=stage,variable=v,n_train=length(ii),observed=obs,
 missing_fraction=missing,distinct=vary,passes_screen=obs>=30 & missing<=.9 & vary>1)}}}
write.csv(do.call(rbind,screening),file.path(out,"training-screening.csv"),row.names=FALSE)

# Audit actual training-only pooling without changing the established algorithm.
pooling<-list()
for(seed in cfg$seeds) {
 tr<-split_train(y,seed);inner<-tr[split_train(y[tr],seed+11,.8)]
 for(stage in c("inner","outer")) {
  ii<-if(stage=="inner")inner else tr
  for(n in names(x))if(is.character(x[[n]])||is.factor(x[[n]])) {
   vv<-x[[n]][ii];if(sum(!is.na(vv))<30 || mean(is.na(vv))>.9 || length(unique(vv[!is.na(vv)]))<2)next
   v<-as.character(vv);v[is.na(v)]<-"Not observed / routed";tt<-table(v)
   rare<-tt[tt<10]
   if(length(rare))pooling[[length(pooling)+1L]]<-data.frame(seed=seed,stage=stage,
    variable=n,response=names(rare),training_n=as.integer(rare))
  }
 }
}
write.csv(do.call(rbind,pooling),file.path(out,"rare-category-training-audit.csv"),row.names=FALSE)

for(a in results)stopifnot(nrow(a$tuning)==9L,
 a$chosen$validation_brier==min(a$tuning$validation_brier),
 setequal(a$tuning$mtry,c("sqrt","fraction20","fraction40")),setequal(a$tuning$node,c(5,20,50)))
boundary_n<-sum(feature_checks$mtry=="fraction40")
validation<-c("NINE FROZEN-GRID FOREST FITS VALIDATED",
 "Primary-release Latino registered reported voters; vote/support routing checked; WEIGHT used without trimming or balancing.",
 "Nested source and encoded-item sets passed for all seeds; identified exclusions absent; ideology retained.",
 "Training-only preprocessing and internal validation; all nine grid cells evaluated for each fit.",
 paste("Maximum SHAP reconstruction error:",format(max(feature_checks$shap_max_error),scientific=TRUE)),
 paste("fraction40 selected in",boundary_n,"of 9 fits; no grid expansion."),
 "All-item rankings and top-50 profiles saved. Signed cells require at least 10 holdout observations.",
 "Measurement review flags: Q315/Q603R2 wording discrepancies, published/local release counts, and remaining truncated labels.")
writeLines(validation,file.path(out,"validation.txt"))
tuning_note<-data.frame(Model=match(sub("_[0-9].*","",feature_checks$run),names(names_pretty)),
 Seed=sub(".*_([0-9]+)_forest_FALSE","\\1",feature_checks$run),
 Option=feature_checks$mtry,Node=feature_checks$node,
 Inner_mtry=feature_checks$inner_mtry,Final_mtry=feature_checks$outer_mtry)
write.csv(tuning_note,file.path(out,"selected-tuning.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
calibration_summary<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(names_pretty),function(s){z<-performance[performance$spec==s,]
 data.frame(Model=paste("Model",match(s,names(names_pretty))),N=fmt(z$n,0),
  Prevalence=fmt(z$prevalence,3),Prediction=fmt(z$mean_prediction,3),
  Intercept=fmt(z$calibration_intercept,2),Slope=fmt(z$calibration_slope,2))}))
write.csv(calibration_summary,file.path(out,"calibration-summary.csv"),row.names=FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()),file.path(out,"session-info.txt"))
```

All nine models passed source-variable exclusions, encoded-item membership,
nesting within each seed, ideology retention, grid selection, and SHAP
reconstruction. Maximum reconstruction error is
**`r format(max(feature_checks$shap_max_error),scientific=TRUE)`**, below $10^{-6}$.
The weighted AUC implementation also passes an independent tied-score check.

```{r}
knitr::kable(tuning_note,row.names=FALSE)
```

The 40% upper boundary was selected in **`r boundary_n` of nine fits**. The grid
was not expanded. Inner and final `mtry` counts differ when the training-specific
encoded feature count differs.

## Calibration diagnostics

```{r}
knitr::kable(calibration_summary,row.names=FALSE)
```

Values are mean [minimum, maximum]. An intercept near zero and slope near one
indicate closer calibration. All nine slopes exceed one, suggesting that the fitted probability contrasts
are too compressed relative to the observed holdout relationship. Model 3
also predicts a higher mean Trump share than observed in every split. The
high AUC values therefore do not establish probability calibration.
No calibration correction is fitted to these holdouts.

## Reproduction and saved outputs

From this QMD's directory, run:

```bash
quarto render cmps2020_latino_trump_analysis.qmd --to pdf
```

R packages `ranger`, `treeshap`, `digest`, and `knitr`, Quarto, and XeLaTeX are
required; package versions are recorded in `session-info.txt`. The source root
defaults to `/Users/jessala/Desktop/Active/Github/ml-latino-vote-2020` and can be
relocated with `CMPS2020_SOURCE`. The raw data and two local documentation checksums
are asserted. An ordinary render recomputes all nine fits. Optional
`CMPS2020_SCRATCH` holds fingerprinted aggregate-only checkpoints during layout
verification; no external preparation or baseline result is required.

The `results/` directory contains aggregate sample, source, disposition, tuning,
performance, calibration, importance, direction, feature, pooling, and validation
records plus three top-50 figures. The QMD, PDF, results directory, and concise
execution note are the persistent deliverables. Forest objects, respondent IDs,
individual predictions and SHAP arrays are never exported. Scratch render files
and aggregate checkpoints are removed after final verification.

